studyKeyFindings: Model skill varied by station and model group; about 33% of sunshine-duration/radiation models and 75% of air-temperature models performed well. Best predictions generally had RMSE below 5 MJ m-2.
studyFutureWorks: Expand long-term ground monitoring and test additional hybrid or machine-learning models.
studyLimits: Ground observations were available at only two stations and reanalysis required bias correction.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked existing empirical models to identify suitable GSR estimators for six Fiji stations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Sparse, spatially variable solar-radiation observations limit renewable-energy assessment in Fiji.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared ERA-Interim reanalysis, eight empirical models and a support vector machine using 2007–2017 observations at Ahvaz, BandarAbbas and Kermanshah, Iran; assessed calibration and validation RMSE.
studyKeyFindings: SVM performed best at Ahvaz and Kermanshah; validation RMSE was 242 and 315 J cm-2 day-1 for best empirical comparators. ERA-Interim was a useful fallback but less accurate.
studyFutureWorks: Test additional machine-learning methods and denser station networks.
studyLimits: Only three Iranian stations and a limited observation period were used.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked reanalysis, empirical and AI models for three representative Iranian stations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Sparse radiation measurements limit daily solar-radiation estimation.

studyMethodsSummary: Evaluated regressions in logs, ARIMA, unobserved-components, transfer functions, neural networks and hybrids on six global-horizontal-radiation datasets at 5, 15, 30 and 60 minute resolutions using true out-of-sample forecasts.
studyKeyFindings: Log-ARIMA with time-varying coefficients performed best in most tests; cloud-cover transfer functions improved high-resolution forecasts, with occasional neural/hybrid gains at 5-minute resolution.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate additional sites and probabilistic forecasts.
studyLimits: Performance depends on site, resolution and weather variability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Systematic out-of-sample comparison across four temporal resolutions.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Few studies compare many time-series approaches across operational high resolutions.

studyMethodsSummary: Comprehensive literature review of environmental impacts from solar thermal/PV, wind, biomass, geothermal, hydroelectric, tidal, ocean, and osmotic power plants, supplemented by SWOT analysis.
studyKeyFindings: Renewable plants reduce carbon emissions but can cause land-use, material, biodiversity, water, noise and marine impacts; impacts vary strongly by technology and site.
studyFutureWorks: Develop consistent comparative environmental indicators and mitigation strategies.
studyLimits: Review findings depend on published life-cycle and case-study evidence.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Synthesized impacts and opportunities/threats across major RES technologies.
studyResearchGapIdentified: RES technologies are often labeled clean while non-CO2 environmental effects receive less attention.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied autoregressive integrated moving average models to long-range total solar irradiance at the top of the atmosphere and surface air-temperature time series.
studyKeyFindings: The same ARIMA model type represented both series; surface temperature closely imitated TSI variability, consistent with random-walk behavior linked to solar activity.
studyFutureWorks: Test additional climate forcings and longer observational records.
studyLimits: Analysis is based on selected long-term series and model assumptions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided a common ARIMA representation for comparing the two series.
studyResearchGapIdentified: The similarity of stochastic variability in solar irradiance and surface temperature needed time-series characterization.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed and tested an adaptive alpha-model using measured sunshine duration, air temperature and relative humidity at Jeddah, Saudi Arabia; predicted global, direct and diffuse irradiance.
studyKeyFindings: Predictions agreed well with measurements, achieving correlation coefficients above 97% and low mean bias error.
studyFutureWorks: Test the adaptive model across climates and longer periods.
studyLimits: Validation focused on one site.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Introduced a meteorology-driven adaptive hourly irradiance predictor.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Conventional irradiance models have limited adaptability to local atmospheric conditions.

studyMethodsSummary: Tested three next-hour GHI forecasting methods at Miami and Orlando: direct GHI ARIMA, separate DHI/DNI ARIMA combined with an atmospheric model, and cloud-cover transient ARIMA with nonlinear regression lookup tables.
studyKeyFindings: Including cloud-cover information improved forecast accuracy relative to irradiance-only approaches.
studyFutureWorks: Validate cloud-cover models across more climates and forecast horizons.
studyLimits: Tests used two US weather stations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Integrated cloud-cover index information into ARIMA and nonlinear-regression forecasts.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Short-term GHI forecasts often omit cloud-transient effects.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied non-seasonal Box-Jenkins ARIMA models to daily averages of wind speed, solar irradiance, ambient air temperature and PV-module temperature in Bahrain’s first hybrid system (4.0 kWp PV and 1.7 kWp wind).
studyKeyFindings: Different ARIMA specifications captured autocorrelation and provided forecasts for hybrid-system operation.
studyFutureWorks: Test seasonal and multivariate models with longer operational records.
studyLimits: Study concerns one hybrid installation and local climate.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Established ARIMA forecasting models for four key hybrid-system signals.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Hybrid-system management requires forecasts of multiple weather and component variables.

studyMethodsSummary: Combined numerical weather prediction inputs with stationary endogenous data, a multilayer perceptron and ARMA residual modeling; tested hourly forecasts at five Mediterranean sites.
studyKeyFindings: Hybrid MLP/ARMA outperformed classical models at all sites, with nRMSE about 14.9%.
studyFutureWorks: Assess transferability to other climates and longer horizons.
studyLimits: Results are based on five Mediterranean locations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Introduced an optimized hybrid ARMA/ANN architecture with pre-input selection.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Classical radiation forecasts did not fully exploit NWP and nonlinear temporal structure.

studyMethodsSummary: Tested two multilayer-perceptron architectures on a two-year hourly irradiation series, comparing endogenous/exogenous inputs against ARMA and persistence baselines.
studyKeyFindings: A multi-output MLP reduced nRMSE by 1.3 points versus ARMA and 7.8 points versus persistence.
studyFutureWorks: Validate across more sites and seasons.
studyLimits: Evaluation used one real-case time series.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Demonstrated a pre-treated multi-output MLP for 24-hour-ahead irradiation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Day-ahead PV forecasts need nonlinear models that use both historical and external information.

studyMethodsSummary: Optimized a multilayer perceptron using pre-treated, stationary multivariate time series for daily global-radiation prediction and assessed alternative network configurations.
studyKeyFindings: The optimized MLP improved daily radiation prediction compared with conventional approaches.
studyFutureWorks: Test robust optimization across additional PV plants.
studyLimits: Performance depends on preprocessing and site-specific data.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided an optimized multivariate MLP workflow for daily radiation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: ANN forecasts require careful stationarity treatment and architecture selection.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed seasonal ARIMA models using hourly solar-radiation observations from Seoul, South Korea, spanning 1981–2017, and evaluated daily and monthly forecasts.
studyKeyFindings: SARIMA represented long-term seasonal patterns and provided accurate daily and monthly global-radiation predictions.
studyFutureWorks: Validate with additional Korean stations and exogenous weather variables.
studyLimits: Single Seoul station and historical data period.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided SARIMA models for both temporal scales.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Few long-term studies jointly forecast daily and monthly radiation with seasonal ARIMA.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared ARMA, nonlinear autoregressive neural network and hybrid ARMA-NAR models for multi-hour hourly and high-frequency solar-radiation forecasts at Ghardaia, Algeria; polynomial detrending was used to stationarize data.
studyKeyFindings: The hybrid ARMA-NAR model improved forecasts by combining linear and nonlinear dynamics.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate additional climates and horizons.
studyLimits: Validation focused on one Algerian site.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined detrended ARMA and NAR neural forecasting.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar series are both nonstationary and nonlinear, limiting single-model forecasts.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied seasonal ARIMA to 34 years of NASA POWER monthly insolation data for the Delhi region and generated four-year forecasts visualized with a marching-square contour algorithm.
studyKeyFindings: Forecast accuracy reached R2 0.9293, RMSE 0.3529, MAE 0.2659 and MAPE 6.556.
studyFutureWorks: Validate forecasts with ground stations and other regions.
studyLimits: Remote-sensing modeled data and one regional case study.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined SARIMA forecasting with spatial contour visualization.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Spatial solar forecasts are rarely presented as operational contour maps.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied ARMA and ARIMA models to stationary and non-stationary monthly mean daily global-radiation series for one-, two- and three-month-ahead forecasts.
studyKeyFindings: Time-series models produced useful multi-month forecasts for large-scale solar-radiation data.
studyFutureWorks: Test hybrid and exogenous-variable models.
studyLimits: Forecast performance depends on stationarity treatment and data source.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared ARMA and ARIMA across multiple forecast horizons.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Few studies address operational multi-month solar forecasts using both stationary and non-stationary formulations.

studyMethodsSummary: Benchmarked autoregressive and machine-learning time-series models using endogenous global-irradiance data at 5-minute, hourly and daily horizons in Algeria.
studyKeyFindings: Model performance varied with temporal resolution and forecast horizon; optimized models were especially effective for hourly forecasts.
studyFutureWorks: Add exogenous weather forecasts and more locations.
studyLimits: Case study limited to Algerian sites and endogenous inputs.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared forecasting approaches across three operational resolutions.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Few benchmarks span sub-hourly, hourly and daily horizons in one study.

studyMethodsSummary: Built supervised Support Vector Machine models combined with time-series inputs for one-hour-ahead global horizontal solar radiation at Ghardaia, Algeria; compared with persistence and published models using RMSE, NRMSE, NMBE, MAPE and correlation.
studyKeyFindings: The selected SVM produced accurate one-hour forecasts and outperformed several benchmark models.
studyFutureWorks: Validate SVM forecasting across climates and horizons.
studyLimits: Single arid-site case study.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Integrated lagged radiation time-series features with supervised SVM learning.
studyResearchGapIdentified: SVM time-series combinations remain underused for in-situ hourly solar forecasting.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a combined linear Box–Jenkins ARMA and nonlinear ANN model using two years of daily global-radiation observations (2012–2013) at two Algerian climate sites.
studyKeyFindings: The combined model improved mean percentage error by 18.1% and 2.7% at one site and 27.26% and 1.39% at the other versus ARMA and ANN, respectively; RMSE reductions were also reported.
studyFutureWorks: Validate with longer records and more climates.
studyLimits: Only two years of data from two sites were analyzed.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined the complementary ARMA and ANN processes for daily radiation estimation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: ARMA and ANN alone do not fully handle both linear and nonlinear solar-radiation dynamics.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained, optimized, validated and independently tested MLP, ANFIS, SVM and decision-tree models in sunshine, temperature, meteorological and day-number input groups using five years of high-resolution measurements from Cairo, Egypt.
studyKeyFindings: MLP models were most accurate, with RMSE 4.75–31.69% lower than the corresponding best regression models; ANFIS and SVM followed, while decision trees demonstrated useful simple temperature/day-number models.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate models across more climates and operational datasets.
studyLimits: One five-year Cairo case study limits geographic transferability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked four machine-learning approaches against regression models on independent data.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Comparative evidence for several machine-learning algorithms and input categories was limited.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared extreme learning machine, backpropagation neural-network, random-forest, generalized regression neural-network and Iqbal empirical models using daily diffuse radiation at Beijing and Zhengzhou stations in the North China Plain.
studyKeyFindings: AI models outperformed the Iqbal model at both stations; the GANN model had the best accuracy, followed by ELM, random forest and GRNN. All models underestimated diffuse radiation.
studyFutureWorks: Extend to more sites and pollution conditions.
studyLimits: Only two stations with diffuse-radiation measurements were assessed.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked AI and empirical methods using measured daily diffuse radiation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Diffuse-radiation observations are scarce in the particulate-polluted North China Plain.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained and tested SVM and XGBoost models with daily global radiation, maximum/minimum temperature, transformed precipitation, and extraterrestrial radiation at three humid-subtropical Chinese stations; compared against four empirical models.
studyKeyFindings: Both machine-learning models outperformed empirical models. Adding precipitation improved RMSE by 5.9–12.2% in training and 8.0–11.5% in testing; XGBoost was generally more accurate, stable and faster than SVM.
studyFutureWorks: Test across climates and additional weather predictors.
studyLimits: Only three humid-subtropical stations and selected input variables were examined.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Evaluated precipitation-enhanced SVM and XGBoost against empirical estimators.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Daily solar radiation is often unmeasured, while commonly available meteorological variables remain underused.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed MLFFNN, RBFNN, SVR, FIS and ANFIS models for hourly irradiance in Abu Musa Island using either local time and meteorological inputs (N1) or past irradiance time-series values (N2).
studyKeyFindings: For N1, SVR and MLFFNN achieved correlation coefficients of 0.9999 and 0.9795, respectively. For N2, SVR, MLFFNN and ANFIS exceeded 0.95 correlation on testing data.
studyFutureWorks: Assess models at diverse climates and with additional predictors.
studyLimits: One island site limits generalizability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared five ML algorithms under meteorological and purely autoregressive input strategies.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Grid integration requires accurate hourly irradiance forecasts from both weather and time-series inputs.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed support vector regression (SVM-R) to estimate daily global solar radiation on a horizontal surface using sunshine ratio alone, trained with 2005–2006 data and tested on 2007 data from Ghardaia, Algeria.
studyKeyFindings: Testing yielded RMSE 1.59 MJ m-2, relative RMSE 8.46%, and correlation coefficient 97.4%, showing SVM-R is effective using only sunshine ratio.
studyFutureWorks: Validate simple-input SVM-R at other sites and climates.
studyLimits: Single site and three-year data record.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided a simple sunshine-ratio SVM-R estimator for DGSR.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Daily global-radiation data are often unavailable in isolated locations.

studyMethodsSummary: Used support vector regression with different combinations of ambient temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, day number and wind speed to estimate GHSR from 2009–2011 NISE data at Gurugram, India; compared with hidden Markov and ANN models using RMSE.
studyKeyFindings: SVR outperformed hidden Markov and ANN comparators; temperature was the most important input, together with pressure, humidity, day number and wind speed.
studyFutureWorks: Validate meteorological-input SVR across Indian climates.
studyLimits: One three-year site-specific dataset.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Evaluated SVR sensitivity to meteorological-input combinations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: PV planning requires GHSR estimates where direct measurements may be unavailable.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed an hourly naïve Bayes classifier for two-day-ahead GHI prediction using public weather forecasts of temperature, relative humidity, dew point and sky coverage, while representing daylight variation and the diurnal cycle.
studyKeyFindings: The naïve Bayes model improved forecast results; over an eight-month test set it achieved RMBE 2.73% relative to mean GHI 333.04 Wh m-2.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate with additional regions and compare operational forecasts.
studyLimits: Results depend on public weather-forecast quality and tested data conditions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Applied a fast NB classifier that accounts for daylight and diurnal GHI characteristics.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Two-day-ahead GHI forecasting needs fast methods using readily available weather forecasts.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared smart persistence, artificial neural networks and random forests for one- to six-hour forecasts of global horizontal, beam normal and diffuse horizontal irradiance measured at Odeillo, France.
studyKeyFindings: Random forest was most efficient; GHI nRMSE ranged 19.65–27.78%, BNI 34.11–49.08%, and DHI 35.08–49.14% across h+1 to h+6 horizons.
studyFutureWorks: Validate solar-component forecasts at additional climates.
studyLimits: Single highly variable meteorological site.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked RF and ANN against smart persistence for three irradiance components.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Component-specific solar forecasts remain challenging under variable meteorological conditions.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS), classification and regression trees (CART), M5 model trees and random forest for one- to six-day-ahead hourly solar-radiation forecasts using a Gorakhpur, India solar-resource dataset.
studyKeyFindings: Random forest delivered the best forecasts while CART performed worst among the four tested models.
studyFutureWorks: Assess models at other sites and incorporate weather forecasts.
studyLimits: Results are based on a single solar-resource site.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked four tree/regression machine-learning methods for horizons up to six days.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Utilities need reliable multi-day hourly solar forecasts for power planning and bidding.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed and tested SVR, ANN and decision-tree base models and their boosting and bagging ensembles using five years of hourly meteorological data from five Turkish cities; evaluated R2 and RMSE.
studyKeyFindings: Boosting and bagging ensembles improved base-model RMSE by 4.6–14.6% on average, demonstrating improved solar-irradiance estimation accuracy.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate ensembles with other algorithms and climates.
studyLimits: Five-city national case study and selected ensemble configurations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared boosting and bagging ensembles of three common regression learners.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Ensemble learning beyond random forests had limited detailed evaluation for solar-irradiance prediction.

studyMethodsSummary: Evaluated neural-network, support-vector-regression and Gaussian-process regressors for hourly global solar radiation at Toledo, Spain using geostationary Meteosat inputs (cloud index and visible reflectivity), clear-sky radiation, and physical-model outputs; compared with Heliosat-2, CAMS and SolarGIS.
studyKeyFindings: Machine-learning regressors provided reliable global-radiation estimates from satellite measurements; using physical-model outputs as post-processing inputs produced the best estimates.
studyFutureWorks: Validate satellite/ML post-processing across regions and years.
studyLimits: One year of data at a single radiometric station.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked regressors and physical models, including physical-model output as ML inputs.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Satellite physical approaches can benefit from data-driven post-processing for local solar-radiation estimation.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared Simple Membership Function and Fuzzy Rule Generating Technique (SMGRT), deep learning and ANFIS using sunshine duration, extraterrestrial radiation, relative humidity, cloudiness, air temperature and soil temperature at Isparta, Turkey (2007–2016 excluding 2010).
studyKeyFindings: All methods performed well, but SMGRT was slightly better. Its Model 1 using H0, sunshine duration and air temperature had MBE 0.156, MSE 1.878, RMSE 1.371 and R2 0.960.
studyFutureWorks: Validate methods at other climates and stations.
studyLimits: Single Turkish station and historical data record.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided a comparative SMGRT, DL and ANFIS evaluation with multiple predictor combinations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Reliable monthly solar-radiation prediction is needed with limited, commonly available meteorological data.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed ANN and recurrent neural-network models from actual meteorological-year data at an Alabama weather station; compared sampling frequencies and moving-window scenarios for solar-radiation prediction.
studyKeyFindings: RNN improved NMBE by 47% and RMSE by 26% versus ANN. Increasing data frequency from one hour to ten minutes reduced CV(RMSE) from 30.9% to 9.41% for ANN and 9.83% to 7.64% for RNN; moving window improved RNN NMBE from 0.9% to 0.2%.
studyFutureWorks: Test more climates, building-control settings, and cloud conditions.
studyLimits: One local weather station limits broader generalization.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared ANN and RNN with data-granularity and moving-window enhancements.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Higher solar-radiation forecast accuracy is needed to support smart-building model predictive control.

studyMethodsSummary: Evaluated SVM, M5 model tree, random forest, XGBoost and CatBoost using six input combinations of daily global radiation, sunshine hours, maximum/minimum temperature and relative humidity from 15 Chinese stations (1996–2015), under limited local and extrinsic-data scenarios.
studyKeyFindings: Without global radiation, average RMSE increased 42.4% across China (68.3% in subtropical/tropical monsoon regions). SVM was most accurate/generalizable, but CatBoost was recommended based on close accuracy and far lower computation time, particularly for extrinsic data.
studyFutureWorks: Test wider data-sharing configurations and future climates.
studyLimits: Station selection and historical data may constrain transferability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared local and extrinsic-data soft-computing models for 15 Chinese stations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Reliable diffuse-radiation prediction is difficult when target stations lack complete or historical local data.

studyMethodsSummary: Implemented multilayer perceptron and radial-basis-function models for up-to-three-step-ahead daily global and direct solar-radiation forecasting using three years of meteorological observations at URAER, Ghardaia (2014–2016).
studyKeyFindings: Both MLP and RBF performed well for three-step-ahead forecasts; MLP showed a slight advantage in statistical metrics.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate at more climates and longer lead times.
studyLimits: A single semi-arid Saharan site and three-year record were used.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared MLP and RBF forecasts of global and direct radiation in Saharan conditions.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Atmospheric changes complicate multi-step solar-component forecasts for grid management.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared ANN, convolutional neural network, recurrent neural network, polynomial regression, support vector regression and random forest for hourly global and diffuse radiation at four Nigerian locations using 12 years of typical meteorological-year data.
studyKeyFindings: Deep-learning models produced more accurate GSR and DSR predictions than machine-learning models, while most machine-learning models trained/tested faster. RNN was best overall for GSR in Yobe (r 0.9546; RMSE/MAE 82.22/36.52 W m-2).
studyFutureWorks: Test on live measurements and assess deployment trade-offs.
studyLimits: Data used typical meteorological years at four Nigerian locations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked deep, standard machine-learning and ensemble methods for both global and diffuse radiation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Model-selection trade-offs between prediction accuracy and computing time need systematic comparison.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained recurrent neural network, long short-term memory and gated recurrent unit models on meteorological data from five Bangladeshi cities to forecast each day’s solar radiation from previous-day weather inputs.
studyKeyFindings: GRU was the best model across the comparison, with MAPE 19.28%.
studyFutureWorks: Test additional locations, weather inputs and longer forecast horizons.
studyLimits: Five cities and available meteorological data constrain wider generalization.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared three recurrent-network architectures across five cities.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Accurate solar-radiation forecasting systems using broad meteorological inputs are scarce in Bangladesh.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a corrected-SVM approach using air temperature as the sole input: one SVM estimates horizontal global solar radiation, another estimates its error, and a weighted sum gives the corrected prediction. Evaluated at semi-arid Ghardaia, Algeria, using 2013–2015 measurements.
studyKeyFindings: Corrected-SVM improved conventional SVM: MABE 1.623 vs 1.713, RMSE 2.286 vs 2.575 MJ m-2, relative error 11.35 vs 12.61%, and correlation 94.20 vs 93.06%.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate corrected SVM in other climates and with additional inputs.
studyLimits: Single semi-arid site and three-year record.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Corrected conventional SVM estimates by modeling and weighting their residual errors.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Daily radiation prediction is needed where only air-temperature measurements are available.

studyMethodsSummary: Used a continuous-density Hidden Markov Model with Pearson R pattern-similarity clustering to select clusters of meteorological inputs, then a Generalized Fuzzy Model to estimate solar radiation. Tested 15 input combinations using 915 days at the Solar Energy Centre, Gurgaon; trained on 750 days and validated on 165.
studyKeyFindings: Sunshine duration was the most important predictor; the best combination used all inputs except wind speed and achieved RMSE 7.9124, MAPE 3.0083 and R 0.9921.
studyFutureWorks: Test the HMM–fuzzy approach at diverse sites.
studyLimits: One monitoring station and a three-year record.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined shape-based HMM clustering with nonlinear generalized fuzzy modeling.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Distance-based clustering and single models may not capture input-pattern similarities for solar-radiation estimation.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a hybrid Coral Reefs Optimization–Extreme Learning Machine model using measured, radiosonde and meteorological-model data at Murcia’s radiometric station; ELM predicts daily global radiation while CRO evolves neural-network weights.
studyKeyFindings: CRO–ELM produced more accurate daily global-radiation predictions than classical ELM and support vector regression.
studyFutureWorks: Validate the optimization–learning approach across sites and seasons.
studyLimits: Single southern-Spain station.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Used Coral Reefs Optimization to evolve ELM weights for daily global-radiation prediction.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Daily solar-radiation predictors require improved nonlinear model optimization from heterogeneous meteorological data.

studyMethodsSummary: Proposed a Genetic Approach Combining Multi-Model Framework: a genetic algorithm dynamically segments the solar series, subsequences are clustered, and a separate time-delay neural network is trained for each pattern. Used 2009 Singapore data for training/tuning and 2010 for validation.
studyKeyFindings: The pattern-specific genetic multi-model framework outperformed comparison algorithms for daily solar-radiation prediction.
studyFutureWorks: Test the adaptive segmentation and pattern identification at other sites.
studyLimits: Validated on a 24-month single-location series.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Used genetic dynamic segmentation, cluster-specific models and pattern identification for forecasting.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Fixed-length segmentation can miss meaningful stochastic solar-radiation patterns.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed Cuckoo Search-Optimally Pruned Extreme Learning Machine (CS-OP-ELM) forecasting models using direct and direct-recursive strategies. MRSR and leave-one-out cross-validation rank and prune feed-forward-neural-network neurons, and Cuckoo Search optimizes weights. Compared with ARMA, back-propagation NN and OP-ELM using US hourly radiation data.
studyKeyFindings: CS-OP-ELM achieved the best forecasting performance among the evaluated methods for clear- and real-sky global horizontal radiation.
studyFutureWorks: Test the optimized hybrid model across additional climates and horizons.
studyLimits: Site count is inconsistently described in the text and performance is based on selected US datasets.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined neuron pruning, two forecasting strategies and Cuckoo Search weight optimization.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation forecasts require efficient nonlinear models with automatic neural-architecture optimization.

studyMethodsSummary: Used monthly mean global solar radiation and 12 meteorological variables from four US sites (1998–2010). Pearson correlations and Apriori association rules selected inputs; radial-basis-function networks were converted to linear regression with hard-ridge node pruning and optimized using Cuckoo Search and Differential Evolution.
studyKeyFindings: The proposed hard-ridge RBF models optimized by Cuckoo Search and Differential Evolution produced more accurate forecasts than the comparison models.
studyFutureWorks: Assess larger station networks and alternative feature-selection methods.
studyLimits: Four US sites and monthly historical records limit generalization.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Introduced hard-ridge penalized and intelligently optimized RBF forecast models.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Sparse radiation observations demand accurate solar prediction from readily available weather variables.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a hybrid self-organizing-map, support-vector-regression and particle-swarm-optimization model. SOM partitions input space into characteristic regions, SVR models each region, and PSO automatically selects SVR parameters; tested in Colorado, USA and Singapore.
studyKeyFindings: The hybrid SOM–SVR–PSO method outperformed traditional hourly solar-irradiance forecasting models.
studyFutureWorks: Validate with other climates and forecast horizons.
studyLimits: Only two locations were reported.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined SOM partitioning, regional SVR models and PSO parameter selection.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Noise, nonstationarity and SVM parameter sensitivity reduce the reliability of statistical irradiance forecasts.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed an SVM–Firefly Algorithm hybrid model using sunshine duration, maximum temperature and minimum temperature to estimate monthly mean horizontal global solar radiation across Iseyin, Maiduguri and Jos, Nigeria; compared against ANN and genetic-programming models.
studyKeyFindings: SVM–FFA was more accurate than ANN and GP. It achieved test RMSE 1.8661, R2 0.7280, correlation 0.8532 and MAPE 11.5192.
studyFutureWorks: Test the hybrid method at more climates and with further meteorological variables.
studyLimits: Three Nigerian sites and historical observations may limit generalizability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Optimized SVM prediction using Firefly Algorithm with three simple meteorological inputs.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Many weather stations lack solar-radiation records despite having routine meteorological data.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a nonlinear SVM with hard penalty function for 30-day global-radiation forecasts at four US sites. Eclat association-rule mining selected meteorological inputs; SVM was converted to a ridge-regularization problem, hard penalty selected radial-basis-function count, and glowworm swarm optimization tuned parameters.
studyKeyFindings: The proposed nonlinear hard-penalty SVM with glowworm optimization gave the best forecasting performance versus competitors.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate model robustness in other climates and operational settings.
studyLimits: Four US sites and selected training/test partitions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined Eclat data mining, hard-penalty SVM basis selection and Glowworm Swarm Optimization.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Grid-connected PV needs accurate daily irradiation forecasts despite sparse radiation observations.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a Firefly Algorithm-optimized random-forest model using hourly sunshine ratio, humidity, ambient temperature, month/day/hour inputs from Subang Meteorological Station in Klang Valley, Malaysia. The algorithm optimized tree and leaf counts; compared with conventional RF, ANN and Firefly-optimized ANN.
studyKeyFindings: Optimal forest contained 493 trees and one leaf per tree. The proposed model achieved RMSE 18.98%, MAPE 6.38% and MBE 2.86%, outperforming the comparator models.
studyFutureWorks: Validate optimized random forest at other climates and longer records.
studyLimits: One-year single-site dataset.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Optimized random-forest complexity with Firefly Algorithm for hourly global-radiation prediction.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Reliable hourly solar-radiation data are needed for designing, sizing and controlling solar-energy systems.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a multi-stage ensemble approach for five-day global horizontal radiation forecasts at four Indian locations. The approach uses two-way interaction modeling, Divide-and-Conquer ensembles, LASSO feature selection selected through cross-validation, and Glowworm Swarm Optimization for individual-model weights.
studyKeyFindings: Training/test experiments at four locations demonstrated the proposed multi-stage ensemble was effective and outperformed competitors.
studyFutureWorks: Test additional sites and operational horizons.
studyLimits: Four locations and selected training/test splits limit generalizability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined interaction modeling, sparse feature selection and optimized ensemble weighting.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Grid-connected PV requires accurate and stable medium-term global-horizontal-radiation forecasts.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied fuzzy regression functions with support vector machines (FRF-SVM) and several kernels to yearly mean daily horizontal global solar-radiation data from Turkey; compared against adaptive neuro-fuzzy and coplot-supported genetic-programming approaches.
studyKeyFindings: FRF-SVM with a Gaussian kernel was robust to outliers and overfitting and gave the most accurate estimates among the compared approaches.
studyFutureWorks: Test fuzzy-SVM generalization in more climates and data regimes.
studyLimits: Results are based on one Turkey regional dataset.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined fuzzy regression functions and SVM kernels for robust global-radiation estimation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation investment decisions require robust long-term estimates in complex terrain and climate, including data with outliers.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a combined artificial-neural-network model whose weights are optimized using a nondominated sorting-based multiobjective bat algorithm (NSMOBA). Statistical and frequent-pattern-growth data-mining methods selected inputs; assessed with monthly solar-radiation and meteorological variables from six US datasets in four experiments.
studyKeyFindings: The combined model was more accurate and stable than individual models. NSMOBA improved both forecasting accuracy and stability compared with a single bat algorithm.
studyFutureWorks: Assess the approach in other regions and operational settings.
studyLimits: Experiments used six US datasets and selected model configurations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined multiple ANN models with NSMOBA weight optimization and data-mined input selection.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation forecasting needs simultaneous accuracy and stability improvement, not accuracy alone.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed an ANN/simulated-annealing hybrid using SA temperature cycling to improve ANN calibration. Models used thousands of daily observations and meteorological parameters from Mashhad, Iran (1995–2014), with validation phases and sensitivity analysis.
studyKeyFindings: ANN/SA accurately predicted daily horizontal solar radiation and outperformed standalone ANN, SVM, existing regression and other machine-learning models.
studyFutureWorks: Test the practical design equation and hybrid calibration across climates.
studyLimits: Data are from one Iranian city.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Used simulated-annealing temperature cycling to calibrate ANN and derived a practical design equation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Daily solar-radiation prediction models need improved calibration and a practical form for solar-system design.

studyMethodsSummary: Estimated solar radiation at eight Iranian target synoptic stations (1974–2014) with support vector regression coupled to Krill-Herd Algorithm optimization and neighboring-station data; compared against classical SVR.
studyKeyFindings: SVR-KHA improved testing accuracy at all target stations. SVR-KHA3 at Isfahan performed best with RMSE 1.98 MJ m-2 day-1, MAPE 7.4%, and R2 0.93.
studyFutureWorks: Test other regions, station densities and climate regimes.
studyLimits: Station-network conditions and historical Iranian data may limit transferability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Integrated neighboring-station data with Krill-Herd-optimized SVR.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Low density, uneven distribution, cost and errors in solar-radiation station data limit accurate estimation.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed ANFIS-muSG by hybridizing ANFIS with Salp Swarm Algorithm and Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm for global solar-radiation prediction across North Dakota locations. Used nine years (2010–2018) of maximum, mean and minimum air temperatures and compared seven ANFIS and metaheuristic variants.
studyKeyFindings: ANFIS-muSG improved RMSE-based accuracy by 25.7–54.8% over other models at the study locations, demonstrating effective temperature-only solar-radiation prediction.
studyFutureWorks: Test hybrid metaheuristics across climates and additional predictors.
studyLimits: North Dakota data and temperature-only predictors constrain transferability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Jointly optimized ANFIS using Salp Swarm and Grasshopper Optimization algorithms.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Accurate solar-radiation prediction is needed from readily available temperature observations where radiation data are sparse.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed SVR-GOA-BAK by combining support vector regression, Boruta feature selection and Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm hyperparameter tuning for GHI forecasting at Saudi Arabian sites.
studyKeyFindings: The hybrid model outperformed standalone SVR by 32.15–39.69% in MAPE across sites; GOA tuning outperformed popular optimizers and reduced manual tuning/overfitting risks.
studyFutureWorks: Test online feature selection and additional climates.
studyLimits: Specific Saudi study sites and simulation conditions may limit transferability.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Automated Boruta feature selection and GOA hyperparameter optimization in an SVR framework.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation variability and uncertainty challenge generalizable GHI forecasts; manual SVR tuning risks overfitting.

studyMethodsSummary: Proposed a hybrid model combining wavelet-transform denoising, CEEMDAN decomposition into intrinsic mode functions, improved Atom Search Optimization and outlier-robust extreme learning machine. IASO uses PWLCM mapping and Lévy flight to optimize ORELM weights and thresholds; compared against ten benchmarks.
studyKeyFindings: Benchmark comparisons verified the proposed WT–CEEMDAN–IASO–ORELM model’s robustness and accuracy for solar-radiation prediction.
studyFutureWorks: Test real-time deployment and wider climatic datasets.
studyLimits: Detailed transferability depends on data settings and benchmark selection.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Denoised/decomposed the series and robustly optimized ORELM using an improved metaheuristic.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation sequence volatility and outliers challenge reliable prediction models.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed CNN-REGST, integrating a CNN with dual-stage stacked regression and a level-1 SVM optimized using HyperOpt. Metaheuristic feature selection chose inputs from global climate models and observations, derived using a marine predator algorithm, for six Queensland solar farms; evaluated year-round and compared with deep, machine-learning and persistence models.
studyKeyFindings: CNN-REGST was significantly more accurate than CNN, LSTM, DNN, ELM, REGST, random forest, gradient boosting, MARS and persistence benchmarks for daily GSR.
studyFutureWorks: Validate broader regions and real-time solar-monitoring implementation.
studyLimits: Study evaluated six Queensland solar farms and available climate/observational predictors.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combined deep convolution, stacked regression, SVM, HyperOpt and metaheuristic feature selection.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Efficient high-accuracy GSR forecasts are needed for grid-integrated solar-energy operations.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed hybrid computational-intelligence models coupling Covariance Matrix Adaptive Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) with Extreme Gradient Boosting and Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines for daily solar radiation. Evaluated using climate parameters at Boromo, Dori, Gaoua and Po stations in Burkina Faso.
studyKeyFindings: Hybrid frameworks improved testing RMSE accuracy by 17.2%, 4.9%, 39.8% and 44.5% at Boromo, Dori, Gaoua and Po, respectively, and showed strong predictive performance.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate the hybrid models across more climates and operational datasets.
studyLimits: Four stations in one sub-Saharan region.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Hybridized CMA-ES with XGB and MARS to construct a robust daily solar-radiation surrogate.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-system design and management require accurate robust daily radiation predictions from climate data.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared feed-forward neural network, three Angstrom-type empirical models, Holt-Winters time series and response surface methodology using pressure, relative humidity, wind speed, ambient temperature and sunshine data for Ankara, Karaman, Kilis and Şırnak, Turkey.
studyKeyFindings: All models achieved R2 0.952–0.993, MAPE below 10%, and RMSE below 2 MJ m-2 day-1. ANN was best overall (mean R2 0.9911; MBE 0.1323 MJ m-2 day-1; RMSE 0.78 MJ m-2 day-1; MAPE 4.9263%; t-stat 0.582), followed by Holt-Winters, RSM and empirical models.
studyFutureWorks: Extend comparison to other climates and real-time forecasting.
studyLimits: Four province case study and monthly inputs.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared representative machine-learning, empirical, time-series and mathematical modeling classes.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-radiation measurements are unavailable at many weather stations, requiring accurate model selection.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained ANN models for solar irradiance on an inclined surface in metropolitan Douala using 30-minute data from the IUT Douala meteorological station (17 January 2019–30 October 2020). Tested variable combinations of temperature, wind speed, humidity and air pressure; data were preprocessed in Excel and modeled in MATLAB with 80/15/5 train/validation/test split.
studyKeyFindings: A logistic sigmoid ANN with 50 hidden neurons achieved a 98.883% correlation coefficient between observed and estimated solar irradiation.
studyFutureWorks: Validate across Central African sites and seasons.
studyLimits: A single station and about two years of data limit spatial and temporal generalization.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Optimized ANN input combinations and hidden-layer activation/size for inclined-surface irradiance.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Erratic irradiance driven by climatic fluctuations makes solar prediction difficult in Central Africa.

studyMethodsSummary: Tested 3D-Var assimilation of SEVIRI radiances from Meteosat Second Generation into WRF-ARW Solar v3.8.1. Compared hourly GHI with ARPA ground data and MSG shortwave irradiance estimates, and cloud coverage with MSG Cloud Mask, in two Italian case studies.
studyKeyFindings: Under clear sky, WRF Solar achieved correlation 0.995. Under cloudy conditions, SEVIRI assimilation improved irradiance/cloud forecasts, reducing one-hour cloud-cover MBE from 41.62 to 20.29 W m-2 and improving the first three forecast hours.
studyFutureWorks: Extend assimilation evaluation across seasons and more forecast cases.
studyLimits: Only two preliminary case studies.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Assimilated MSG/SEVIRI radiances in WRF Solar with 3D-Var to improve short-range forecasts.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Variable solar generation requires reliable high-resolution short-term irradiance forecasts for operations.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a hybrid WRF numerical-weather-prediction and clearness-index-based Kalman filter model. Evaluated on one-year photovoltaic-plant solar-radiation data at Maizuru, Japan and Qinghai, China under different sky conditions.
studyKeyFindings: The hybrid method surpassed WRF alone. Under clear skies, MBE accuracy improved 95.7% in Maizuru and 90.9% in Qinghai; RMSE accuracy improved 42.2% and 26.8%, respectively.
studyFutureWorks: Test more climates and sudden-error-change conditions.
studyLimits: Two PV plant sites and one-year datasets.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Corrected WRF forecasts with a clearness-index Kalman filter.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Day-ahead solar forecasts are essential for grid balancing, dispatch, scheduling and trading, but standard Kalman filters miss sudden error changes.

studyMethodsSummary: Modeled a PV panel with a boost converter and MPPT controller in PSIM. Implemented incremental conductance and Kalman-filter algorithms in C/PSIM C blocks, then simulated under stable and variable environmental conditions.
studyKeyFindings: Kalman-filter MPPT outperformed incremental conductance in response time, efficiency and steady-state oscillations.
studyFutureWorks: Validate both algorithms on physical PV hardware.
studyLimits: Simulation study; performance depends on modeled system and test conditions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compared Kalman filtering with incremental conductance in a simulated boost-converter PV system.
studyResearchGapIdentified: PV systems require fast and stable maximum-power tracking under variable irradiance and temperature.

studyMethodsSummary: Conducted twin experiments applying Local Ensemble Transform Kalman Filter (LETKF) data assimilation to the ENLIL solar-wind model. Wang-Sheeley-Arge supplied boundary conditions; synthetic density, temperature and momentum observations were generated every 4.5 hours at 0.6 AU.
studyKeyFindings: LETKF improved modeled state at the observation point and forecast skill near Earth for observed and unobserved variables, but assimilating a single spatial observation created artificial wave-like gradients that propagated Earthward.
studyFutureWorks: Use remote solar-wind observations and address spurious gradients for operational assimilation.
studyLimits: Synthetic data and a single-observation configuration limit operational conclusions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: First in-depth application of advanced NWP-style data assimilation to solar-wind forecasting.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Data assimilation is underused in solar-wind prediction because of limited observations and technical challenges.

studyMethodsSummary: Described and validated a satellite-image intraday solar forecast over three years in Paris for horizons up to six hours. Assessed clear-sky index, solar zenith angle, 10 km surrounding cloud patterns and North Atlantic weather regimes as predictors of forecast uncertainty.
studyKeyFindings: Forecast skill was positive versus persistence (up to 15%) and NWP (20–40%). Error increased as solar zenith angle and clear-sky index decreased; Atlantic Ridge had highest and Scandinavian Blocking lowest errors, with relative RMSE gaps of 8–10% in summer and 18–30% by horizon.
studyFutureWorks: Extend reliability predictors to other regions and integrate them with operational forecast systems.
studyLimits: Validation is specific to Paris and satellite coverage.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Identified weather, cloud and irradiance predictors of satellite-forecast reliability.
studyResearchGapIdentified: PV penetration needs accurate intraday forecasts and advance knowledge of uncertainty driven by evolving clouds.

studyMethodsSummary: Proposed a Kalman-filter PV-power prediction model based on forecasting experience. Hourly solar-irradiance forecasting, NWP data and a photoelectric conversion model generate ground-irradiance/PV-power forecast experience; fitted Kalman dynamics and measured power iteratively correct prediction error. Evaluated using DKASC data simulation.
studyKeyFindings: The proposed model reduced error variability and provided more accurate ultra-short-term PV-power predictions than comparison approaches in DKASC simulations.
studyFutureWorks: Validate in real PV energy-storage power stations.
studyLimits: Evidence is simulation-based and depends on forecast-experience/model assumptions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Fused NWP-driven forecast experience with Kalman error correction using measured power.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Historical-experience PV forecasts lose accuracy during anomalous conditions, and photoelectric conversion equations are difficult to model directly.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained LSTM networks to predict solar irradiation and temperature over 24 hours from MERRA-2 hourly temperature, relative humidity, pressure, wind speed/direction, irradiation and rainfall data for 20 northern Cameroon locations, 2000–2022; tested at Makary and Banyo.
studyKeyFindings: LSTM prediction achieved 92.45% accuracy and RMSE 20.9. Average solar-energy potential was 2.193 MWh m-2 year-1 at Makary and 1.949 at Banyo, supporting solar-plant, PV/EV fleet and charging-station site selection.
studyFutureWorks: Validate predictions against local measurements and expand EV deployment analysis.
studyLimits: Reanalysis-based analysis and testing at two highlighted localities.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Used 23 years of MERRA-2 data and LSTM predictions to map resource potential across 20 locations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Northern Cameroon needs solar-resource forecasts and potential estimates to support PV and solar-EV development.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied the Capderou theoretical method with Klein day calculations to determine hourly global, direct and diffuse solar-radiation components on horizontal and inclined surfaces across all months in N’Djamena, Chad.
studyKeyFindings: Hourly component estimates across January–December agreed satisfactorily with comparable literature values, supporting Capderou-method application outside a desert climate.
studyFutureWorks: Establish ground monitoring and validate the model across Chad.
studyLimits: No countrywide solar-radiation measurement network was available for direct validation.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provided a theoretical Capderou correlation model for global, direct and diffuse radiation on horizontal and tilted planes.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Chad lacks meteorological stations to measure solar radiation throughout the country.

studyMethodsSummary: Applied a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making Analytic Hierarchy Process and GIS to assess wet-cooled grid-connected CSP suitability across Cameroon. Criteria included DNI, temperature, slope, elevation, distances to grid/roads/railways/homes/watercourses and land use; evaluated technical, socio-economic and equal-weight scenarios.
studyKeyFindings: 42.35% of land was unsuitable; 44% suitable, 13.46% highly suitable and 0.01% most suitable. Far North contained highly suitable areas. Standard-scenario theoretical potential was 37,917.005 TWh/year, varying across sensitivity scenarios.
studyFutureWorks: Incorporate refined population density, security indicators and minimum surface-area constraints.
studyLimits: Results depend on criteria weights, spatial datasets and CSP technical assumptions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Integrated AHP weighting and GIS mapping to rank CSP site suitability and theoretical potential.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Cameroon needs transparent, spatially explicit CSP site-selection and potential estimates for grid-connected projects.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared physical and machine-learning models at each solar-power modeling step—global horizontal irradiance, direct normal irradiance, global tilted irradiance and PV power—using hourly Seoul data from April 2011 to December 2017.
studyKeyFindings: With suitable inputs, ML models generally outperformed physical models and substantially reduced mean bias difference: GHI MBD 0.96% and PV-power MBD 0.03%. LSTM and GRU were recommended ML models, while physical PV-power models reduced RMSD more efficiently.
studyFutureWorks: Test other climates and assess hybrid physical/ML model combinations.
studyLimits: Results use a Seoul dataset and model performance depended on selected inputs.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Systematically compared physical and ML approaches from irradiance components through PV power.
studyResearchGapIdentified: No prior study had compared machine-learning accuracy with physical models at every stage of solar-power modeling.

studyMethodsSummary: Evaluated six empirical models for global solar radiation on a horizontal surface at Abeche, Chad using data from the General Directorate of National Meteorology of Chad; used statistical indicators and NASA data validation to identify the most accurate model.
studyKeyFindings: The Sabbagh model performed best, estimating an average 6.354 kWh m-2 with average deviation −3.704%, and was validated against NASA data.
studyFutureWorks: Extend testing to more Chadian sites and compare modern ML models.
studyLimits: One site and empirical models only.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarked six empirical models against meteorological and NASA data for Abeche.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Reliable local solar-radiation estimates are needed to support renewable-energy planning in Chad.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed and simulated an Environmental Sensor-less Hybrid Analytical-Machine Learning (ESHAML) framework combining a PV analytical model, Bayesian-regularized neural network temperature approximation, synthetic data generation, and fractional-area MPPT; experimentally validated it with an IoT Trio-PV Monitor in Dschang, Cameroon.
studyKeyFindings: ESHAML achieved 2.668–3.561% simulated MAPE and 4.9355% experimental MAPE, with MPPT convergence below 20 ms; its experimental MAPE outperformed Moshksar & Ghanbari (34.96%) and Abe et al. (7%).
studyFutureWorks: Validate at additional sites and PV configurations and deploy the framework for wider real-time PV applications.
studyLimits: Validation was conducted at one Cameroon site for three consecutive days; reported results depend on the studied PV setup and atmospheric conditions.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provides a sensorless hybrid PV/ML estimator with synthetic-data training and fast MPPT for real-time operation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Costly environmental-sensor dependence, data scarcity, integration complexity, and insufficient real-time accuracy hinder solar-irradiance estimation in resource-constrained regions.

studyMethodsSummary: Used 2015 HelioClim-3 satellite-derived global horizontal irradiation and the Liu–Jordan isotropic model to calculate direct solar radiation on horizontal and south-facing 15° inclined planes for Abeche, Aozou, Faya-Largeau, Moundou, and N’Djamena, Chad.
studyKeyFindings: Northern Chad had higher direct solar radiation than the south; Moundou had the lowest values. Peak irradiance reached 800 W/m² around 11:00–13:00. Reported annual average direct solar radiation was at least 1800 kWh/m²/year, indicating favorable concentrating-solar resource.
studyFutureWorks: Use the estimated resource to support thermo-solar plant siting and incorporate additional measured data.
studyLimits: Results are modelled satellite-data estimates for 2015 rather than direct radiometric-station observations.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Estimates direct radiation for five representative Chad locations from satellite data and a geometric radiation model.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Sparse radiometric and meteorological stations leave Chad’s solar climate and direct radiation poorly characterized.

studyMethodsSummary: Used Weka to select mean solar irradiation, maximum temperature, and measurement time; trained a feed-forward multilayer perceptron ANN using Levenberg–Marquardt on 70% of measured Gandon meteorological data and tested it across twelve 30–360 minute horizons.
studyKeyFindings: Forecast performance declined modestly as the horizon increased. The 360-minute horizon achieved R=0.961 and RMSE=0.075; the authors conclude six-hour forecasting is feasible.
studyFutureWorks: Extend the multi-horizon approach to Senegal’s other regions.
studyLimits: The model was evaluated at one north-west Senegal site and with the reported meteorological measurements.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Provides and compares twelve ANN forecasts from 30 minutes to six hours.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Existing Senegal solar forecasts generally use a single short horizon, limiting investors’ ability to select forecasting windows that match demand and available data.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared three-, four-, and five-parameter PV equivalent-circuit models with NOCT and Sandia cell-temperature models. Calibrated models from manufacturer datasheets and experimental I–V data, then tested monocrystalline and polycrystalline 245 Wp modules with actual weather measurements at SolarTechLab, Politecnico di Milano.
studyKeyFindings: Hourly forecast errors were usually below 15 Wh. No clear advantage of greater circuit complexity was found; calibration data and thermal model mattered more. Sandia with experimental calibration was most accurate for monocrystalline cells, while NOCT with manufacturer data performed better for polycrystalline cells. Errors could be below 1% NMAE and 2% WMAE.
studyFutureWorks: Compare the physical models with neural-network methods and account for PV ageing through recalibration every one or two years.
studyLimits: Predictions used actual weather measurements, excluding weather-forecast error, and evaluations concerned the tested module types and site.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compares physical circuit and thermal models using both datasheet and measured calibration for mono- and polycrystalline modules.
studyResearchGapIdentified: PV power-model accuracy depends on circuit complexity, temperature estimation, and calibration data, but their comparative effects across cell types were unclear.

studyMethodsSummary: Ran WRF at 27-, 9-, and 3-km nested resolution over Singapore for 2015–2016; compared WRF-only, 3DVAR, and 4DVAR initialisations using ground, satellite, and GPS observations. Post-processed forecasts with a 500-tree random forest trained in 2015 and tested in 2016.
studyKeyFindings: Raw 4DVAR had the lowest RMSE (216 W/m², 46% relative RMSE) versus 3DVAR (237 W/m²) and WRF-only (263 W/m²). After random-forest post-processing, 4DVAR remained best (173 W/m², 37% relative RMSE) and all NWP methods outperformed climatology and persistence ensemble.
studyFutureWorks: Assess ensemble or hybrid 3DVAR/EnKF/EMOS methods and examine high-error overcast events.
studyLimits: Overcast conditions had very large errors; 4DVAR was computationally costlier than 3DVAR and the comparison was evaluated in Singapore.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Assimilates ground, satellite, and GPS observations into WRF with 3DVAR and 4DVAR, then compares their next-day irradiance forecasts.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Initial-condition errors limit tropical NWP solar forecasts; Singapore WRF forecasts had not compared 3DVAR and 4DVAR assimilation for next-day irradiance.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that combines a dynamic PV thermal model and sinusoidal irradiation-state model to estimate module temperature and effective irradiation from PV measurements. Used its state estimates in a state-based MPPT controller and simulated 250 W PV performance with one-minute National Wind Technology Center weather data for clear, partly cloudy, and severely cloudy days.
studyKeyFindings: EKF temperature estimates were generally within 2 K and irradiation estimates within 10 W/m² of true values. The state-based MPPT stayed within 2 W of maximum power and increased daily energy by approximately 1%, 5%, and 8.5% over incremental conductance for clear, partly cloudy, and severely cloudy cases respectively.
studyFutureWorks: Validate the estimator/controller experimentally and consider additional PV model effects.
studyLimits: Validation was simulation-based using a simplified lumped PV thermal model; long-wave radiation was neglected.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Uses a feedback EKF to estimate both PV states and supplies them to a state-based MPPT controller.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Temperature and irradiation estimation and MPPT have usually been treated separately, with many methods requiring costly sensors or lacking observer feedback.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed a hybrid nowcaster that fuses a time-varying Kalman-filter predictor and multiple regressor. A support-vector-machine ramp-down classifier uses all-sky-image features and irradiance history; three local-RMSE fusion alternatives were evaluated with four-fold cross-validation on 2014 Taiwan data.
studyKeyFindings: Fusion alternative 2, which selects the Kalman prediction only when its local RMSE is below a threshold, was more stable and generally outperformed alternatives 1 and 3, standalone regressor, fixed/time-varying Kalman filter, and compared neural network. Accuracy degraded only slightly between 10- and 20-minute horizons.
studyFutureWorks: Apply the hybrid mechanism to other sites and nowcasting conditions.
studyLimits: Evaluated at one marine-climate site; numerical chart values were not tabulated in the paper text.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Combines adaptive Kalman and regression predictions according to recent local RMSE and anticipated ramp-down events.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Cloud movement and ramp-down events make high-resolution irradiance nowcasting difficult; individual Kalman or regression predictors excel under different irradiance variability.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared FoBa, leapForward, spikeslab, Cubist, and bagEarthGCV endogenous machine-learning models using minute-resolution NREL solar irradiance data from 2010–2015. Used 70/30 training/testing, same-month historical samples, seasonal 2016 test days, and 1-, 24-, and 48-hour forecast horizons.
studyKeyFindings: Spikeslab and Cubist were most promising and stable across seasons and horizons. Best 48-hour result was spikeslab on 30 August (91.67% accuracy, R=0.92, RMSE=22.73); unstable June weather had lower accuracy and higher error.
studyFutureWorks: Extend the machine-learning forecasting approach with additional inputs and locations.
studyLimits: One NREL site and historical irradiance-only endogenous modelling; effectiveness depends on weather and input-data selection.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Systematically compares five machine-learning methods and historical-data configurations across seasonal 1–48 hour forecasts.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Solar-resource seasonal variability and uncertain selection of historical days/time slots make reliable multi-horizon irradiance prediction difficult.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained a four-dense-layer deep neural network with one dropout layer, mean-square-error loss, Adadelta optimisation, and five-fold cross-validation. Tested 16 input combinations of extraterrestrial radiation, sunshine duration, cloud cover, minimum temperature, and maximum temperature using daily data from 34 Turkish stations (2001–2007).
studyKeyFindings: The all-input C16 model was best overall: R²=0.980, RMSE=0.78 MJ/m²/day, and MAE=0.61 MJ/m²/day. Sunshine duration was the strongest input; cloud cover was second, while temperature added smaller gains. The best station result was Kirikkale (R²=0.992, MAE=0.40, RMSE=0.52).
studyFutureWorks: Apply the model to similar regions and additional solar-radiation estimation settings.
studyLimits: Performance is based on Turkish station data and selected daily meteorological/astronomical inputs.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Evaluates deep learning across a nationally distributed 34-station dataset and input combinations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Sparse or unreliable solar-radiation measurements require accurate estimation from routinely available meteorological and astronomical variables.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared time-series LSTM, ConvLSTM, CNN, random forest, support vector regression, and XGBoost models using hourly Johannesburg temperature, solar irradiance, and sunshine-duration data. Cleaned 2009–2018 Meteoblue records, removed nighttime zeros, used 80/20 training/testing, and varied training data from four months to ten years.
studyKeyFindings: ConvLSTM was best: nRMSE=4.05% for 80% of one year at 500 epochs and 1.51% using ten years. With a one-year dataset, LSTM, XGBoost, SVR, RF, and CNN nRMSE values were 4.72%, 6.63%, 7.8%, 19.8%, and 12.61%, respectively.
studyFutureWorks: Deploy ConvLSTM forecasts in solar farms to support stable PV-grid operation.
studyLimits: Performance depends on local weather, training data size, and model parameters; evaluation used historical Johannesburg data.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarks ConvLSTM alongside five AI methods using historical city weather data.
studyResearchGapIdentified: ConvLSTM had not been compared with LSTM, CNN, and conventional machine-learning models for hourly solar irradiance forecasting using Johannesburg data.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared support vector machine, feed-forward back-propagation ANN, kernel nearest neighbor, and deep learning using daily minimum/maximum temperature, cloud cover, extraterrestrial radiation, and day length for Kırklareli, Tokat, Nevşehir, and Karaman. Turkish State Meteorological Service data from 2018–2019 were randomly split 70%/30% for training/testing and evaluated with seven metrics.
studyKeyFindings: ANN was best overall, followed by deep learning, SVM, and k-NN. Overall best ANN metrics were R²=0.932, RMSE=2.157 MJ/m², rRMSE=14.10%, MABE=1.597 MJ/m², MBE=0.195 MJ/m², t-stat=1.280, and MAPE=15.92%. k-NN was generally worst; Nevşehir was most predictable and Tokat least predictable.
studyFutureWorks: Evaluate additional attributes and regions to refine algorithm selection.
studyLimits: Four Turkish provinces and two years of data; performance varied with province and metric.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Benchmarks four algorithms with seven metrics across four provinces spanning Turkey’s solar-radiation range.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Most solar-radiation stations lack measurement equipment, while different machine-learning models can have close and region-dependent results that require multi-metric comparison.

studyMethodsSummary: Built two single-hidden-layer feed-forward ANN models in MATLAB Simulink with 1–15 neurons and Levenberg–Marquardt, resilient back-propagation, and scaled conjugate gradient training. Used NREL hourly direct/global irradiation, weather, and location attributes for six Tamil Nadu districts; Model 1 trained on five districts and tested on Vellore, while Model 2 used an 80/20 split across all districts.
studyKeyFindings: Model 1 with Levenberg–Marquardt and 12 hidden neurons was best, with R=0.9376 training and R=0.9340 testing. Its testing MAD, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE were 0.045632, 0.005781, 0.076342, and 0.484634, respectively. Model 1 was more stable than Model 2.
studyFutureWorks: Apply the ANN model to estimate hourly radiation at comparable locations without monitoring facilities.
studyLimits: Study covered six hot-area Tamil Nadu locations, one year of data, and the selected inputs/models.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Develops and selects an ANN configuration that estimates hourly direct and global radiation from readily available meteorological and locational inputs.
studyResearchGapIdentified: High acquisition and maintenance cost of meteorological instruments leave many locations without solar-radiation records for PV design.

studyMethodsSummary: Trained and tested standalone ANFIS and hybrid ANFIS-PSO, ANFIS-GA, and ANFIS-DE models on monthly sunshine duration, maximum/minimum temperature, rainfall, and clearness index. Used 108 Kuala Terengganu months (2006–2014) with an 80/20 split and applied the models to Penang Island.
studyKeyFindings: ANFIS-PSO was best. At Kuala Terengganu it achieved test RMSE=0.3065, RRMSE=1.7933%, r=0.9963, R²=0.9921, MABE=0.2482, and MAPE=1.4097%. All models had RRMSE below 10%; ANFIS-GA had longest execution time while standalone ANFIS was fastest.
studyFutureWorks: Expand the monthly solar-radiation database, calibrate models in other regions, and optimise execution time.
studyLimits: Model performance requires the specified meteorological inputs and was evaluated for two Malaysian sites.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Uses routine meteorological variables with ANFIS and three optimisation hybrids, then validates at a second Malaysian site.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Malaysia has missing or scarce solar-radiation records due to costly, complex measurement equipment, and comprehensive high-accuracy hybrid ANFIS monthly models for tropical settings were lacking.

studyMethodsSummary: Compared satellite-derived GHI datasets with ground measurements from 22 cities in six countries, selected SolarGIS based on lowest error, and used pvPlanner to assess optimally tilted crystalline silicon, amorphous silicon, and CIS PV at 33 Cameroon locations. Calculated energy output, performance ratio, capacity factor, simple payback, and LCOE under cost, discount-rate, and generation scenarios.
studyKeyFindings: SolarGIS had the lowest RMSE (7.9%). a-Si produced the highest energy output, PR, and CF across Cameroon. Adjusted annual output ranged 1053–1764 kWh/kWp. At 1500 €/kWp, 5% discount and 1764 kWh/kWp/year, payback was 5.6 years and LCOE was 6.79 €c/kWh; at 2500 €/kWp, 10%, and 1053 kWh/kWp/year, they were 15.7 years and 28.82 €c/kWh.
studyFutureWorks: Facilitate PV deployment in commercial buildings and adopt policies such as duty exemptions, low-interest loans, and tax breaks.
studyLimits: SolarGIS data had 7.9% average GHI overestimation and no reliable Cameroon surface-observation network; economics rely on assumed costs, tariffs, degradation, and demand profile.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Validates satellite datasets using neighbouring-country observations and quantifies location-specific PV energy performance and investment economics in Cameroon.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Cameroon lacks reliable weather observations and PV performance data, limiting resource assessment and investment confidence.

studyMethodsSummary: Downloaded four years of hourly PVGIS/ERA5 data for a 20 kW Bamenda PV system, preprocessed 35,064 records to 33,000, split 80/20 for training/testing, and trained/validated/tested 24 MATLAB Regression Learner models from six technique families. Compared hold-out (25% of training held out) and re-substitution validation using RMSE and R².
studyKeyFindings: Wide neural network was best on hold-out testing with RMSE=9.377 W and R²=0.999; Matérn 5/2 GPR (9.452 W) and exponential GPR (10.299 W) followed. Fine Gaussian SVM was least accurate (RMSE=458.97 W, R²=0.990). Hold-out validation was more accurate for 62% of models.
studyFutureWorks: Deploy the selected model to the cloud for real-time forecasting and evaluate at additional locations.
studyLimits: Data are PVGIS satellite/reanalysis estimates for a single location; findings cannot be generalised and the model was only used within MATLAB.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compares 24 ML models and validation methods on PVGIS data to choose a dependable Bamenda SPVP forecaster.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Cameroon has little machine-learning solar-PV forecasting research and lacks ground measurements with all required inputs/outputs for Bamenda.

studyMethodsSummary: Developed location-specific quadratic relations between diffuse-to-global radiation ratio and clearness index using 1985–2005 HelioClim-1 monthly mean daily horizontal-surface data for Ngaoundéré, Garoua-Boulai, Bafoussam, and Nkambé. Compared results with Page, Liu–Jordan, Iqbal, and Erbs models using MBE, RMSE, and t-statistic.
studyKeyFindings: The proposed quadratic models achieved diffuse-fraction R² of 0.983–0.989 and t-statistics within the 95% critical range, giving closest agreement with observations. Existing models consistently underestimated diffuse radiation and had t-statistics outside the critical range.
studyFutureWorks: Use the location-specific model as a diffuse solar-radiation data-generation scheme where observations are absent.
studyLimits: Analysis relies on satellite-derived monthly mean data and four cities between 5°N and 10°N.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Derives and validates four local clearness-index quadratic models for diffuse-radiation estimation.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Global and diffuse solar radiation are not measured by Cameroon meteorological stations, and existing general diffuse-radiation models may not represent local conditions.

studyMethodsSummary: Estimated Bambili hourly irradiance with Angstrom–Prescott, Kaplanis, Duffie and Beckman, and Collares-Pereira and Rabl models; estimated temperature with WAVE, Parton and Logan, and SOYGRO; then computed PV-module energy output and compared results with NASA data, PVGIS, and PVsyst.
studyKeyFindings: Collares-Pereira and Rabl gave the lowest irradiance RMSE (6.71%). Parton and Logan performed best from 6 a.m. to noon (7.17% RMSE), while SOYGRO was preferred from 1 to 6 p.m. (9.86% RMSE). Estimated annual module energy ranged from 193.29 to 345.87 kWh.
studyFutureWorks: Incorporate environmental disturbances such as sudden cloudiness and rain to improve estimates.
studyLimits: Bambili has no meteorological station; NASA data are satellite-derived rather than local ground measurements.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Applies day-of-year mathematical models to estimate irradiance, temperature, and PV energy output.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Irradiance and temperature data are scarce in Bambili because meteorological stations are unavailable.

studyMethodsSummary: Evaluated Hargreaves and Samani, Annandale, Bristow and Campbell, and Goodin temperature-based regressions for daily global solar radiation at two Cameroon and two Senegal localities. Used RMSE, MBE, t-statistic, coefficient of determination, and Willmott concordance index.
studyKeyFindings: Annandale performed best in Yaounde; Goodin performed best in Garoua, Dakar, and Gandon. Annandale and Goodin estimates were statistically significant at the 99% confidence level where their calculated t values were below 2.5758.
studyFutureWorks: Apply the simple temperature-based models for solar-system design where only air-temperature data are available.
studyLimits: Ground radiation measurements were unavailable for Garoua and Dakar; satellite-based NASA data were used for validation at those sites.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Compares four empirical temperature-based regressions across representative Cameroon and Senegal locations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Observed global solar-radiation data and records are unavailable at many developing-country localities.

studyMethodsSummary: Analysed HelioClim3-v5 satellite global, diffuse, and direct solar-radiation data; in-situ meteorological observations; and SAFNWC cloud classes for Douala. Applied hierarchical clustering with Euclidean distance and Ward aggregation to hourly global-solar-radiation diurnal cycles.
studyKeyFindings: Douala has a bright dry DJF season (~5000 Wh/m²/day), a dark rainy JJAS season (<3500 Wh/m²/day), and two semi-illuminated transition seasons. Five diurnal radiation-cycle types represent 42%, 14%, 18%, 16%, and 10% of the 4017 analysed days.
studyFutureWorks: Quantify cloudiness and aerosol effects and analyse regional climate response.
studyLimits: Further work is needed to quantify cloudiness and aerosol effects on the solar-irradiation balance.
studyResearchGapAddressed: Characterizes seasonal and daily solar-radiation profiles and their cloud-cover associations.
studyResearchGapIdentified: Douala requires a local characterization of annual and diurnal solar-radiation variability and its meteorological drivers.

studyMethodsSummary: Proposed a wind-CSP-electric-heater hybrid, formulated day-ahead scheduling as a MILP with energy-flow, TES, power-block, electric-heater and curtailment constraints, and tested clear-sky, partial-cloudy and annual cases.
